comments.text:
Guess on why the voice cloning happens:
Since I assume 4o is still just a next token predictor, it sometimes gets confused as to whether the "agent" has started speaking.
In conversations with LLMs, I think they typically use some background system prompts to let the LLM know when the human user is speaking, and when the agent that it's supposed to be playing the part of is speaking.
4o sometimes misses the fact that the agent is supposed to be talking, so it outputs in the role of the human, attempting to continue what they were saying in their own voice - because if the human is (supposedly) still talking, the tokens output should be mimicking them as closely as possible since behaviours matching the human's previous behaviours and speaking style are the most likely next tokens.
